nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of needle-like Co(OH)2 precursor
nodes.procedure: In a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave with a capacity of 100 mL, 5.0 mmol of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 30.0 mmol of CO(NH₂)₂, and 12.5 mmol of NH₄F were dissolved in 50.0 mL of DI water. Subsequently, a thoroughly cleaned and dried piece of NF (10×50 mm², thickness: 1.0 mm; aperture: 0.1 mm; porosity: 97.2%) was immersed in the solution. The hydrothermal reaction was maintained at 120°C for 6 h. Then, the obtained n·Co(OH)₂@NF precursor was washed with DI water and ethanol.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfidation of needle-like Co3S4
nodes.procedure: In a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave with a capacity of 100 mL, 1 g of Na₂S·9H₂O was dissolved in 40 mL of DI water. Subsequently, the n-Co(OH)₂@NF precursor (10×10 mm², thickness: 1.0 mm; aperture: 0.1 mm; porosity: 97.2%) was immersed in the solution. The Teflon-lined stainless autoclave was maintained at 90°C for 12 h. Then, the obtained n·Co₃S₄@NF was washed with DI water and ethanol.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of rod-like Co(OH)2 precursor
nodes.procedure: In a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave with a capacity of 100 mL, 1.45 g of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1.5 g of HMT, and 0.37 g of NH4F were dissolved in 50 ml of DI water. Subsequently, a thoroughly cleaned and dried piece of NF (10×50 mm^2, thickness: 1.0 mm; aperture: 0.1 mm; porosity: 97.2%) was immersed in the solution. The Teflon-lined stainless autoclave was maintained at 95°C for 24 h. Upon completion of the reaction, the resulting r·Co(OH)2@NF precursor was washed with DI water and ethanol.

nodes.name: Pt/C electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of 20 wt% Pt/C powder, 500 μL of ethanol, and 50 μL of Nafion were sonicated for 30 min. Next, 100 μL of the above dispersion solution was slowly dropped on cleaned NF (10×10 mm^2, thickness: 1.0 mm; aperture: 0.1 mm; porosity: 97.2%) and dried in air for 10 h to prepare the Pt/C/NF electrode.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of 20 wt% Pt/C/NF... dried in air for 10 h to prepare the Pt/C/NF electrode.

nodes.name: RuO2 electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of 20 wt% RuO2 powder, 500 μL of ethanol, and 50 μL of Nafion were sonicated for 30 minutes. Next, 100 μL of the above dispersion solution was slowly dropped on cleaned NF (10×10 mm^2, thickness: 1.0 mm; aperture: 0.1 mm; porosity: 97.2%) and dried in air for 10 h to prepare the RuO2/NF electrode.

Tafel slope of 94 mV dec⁻¹... charge transfer resistance of 0.82 Ω... chronoamperometry at 524 mV for 240 h, in which the electrolyte was changed every 24 h

The electrocatalytic HER performance... in 1 M NaOH electrolyte... overpotential of n·Co₃S₄@NF (311 mV)... Tafel slopes... 87 mV dec⁻¹... R_ct ≈ 22.8 Ω... Faradaic efficiency of hydrogen production... 99.2%

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks at 26.3°, 31.5°, 38.4°, 47.1°, 50.3°, and 55.0° match spinel-structured Co3S4 (JCPDS 47-1738), with peaks at 44.7°, 52.0°, and 76.6° from Ni substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XRD pattern of the n·Co3S4@NF (Supplementary Fig. 4a), the diffraction peaks at 26.3°, 31.5°, 38.4°, 47.1°, 50.3°, and 55.0° are well matched with the spinel-structured Co3S4 (JCPDS 47-1738)

nodes.characterization_summary: n·Co3S4@NF shows needle-like morphology with length-width ratio of ca. 20:1 and tip structure; r·Co3S4@NF shows rod-like morphology with length-width ratio of ca. 4:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Co 2p shows peaks at 798.30 and 782.20 eV (Co2+) and 796.70 and 781.46 eV (Co3+) with satellite peaks; S 2p peaks at 168.89 eV (SO4^2-), 164.00 eV (S 2p1/2), 161.83 eV (S 2p3/2). Co2+ peak shifts 0.29 eV leftward relative to precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p of the n·Co3S4@NF catalyst can be deconvoluted into two pairs of spin-orbit double peaks (Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2) with satellite peaks (Sat.). The peaks at 798.30 and 782.20 eV correspond to Co2+ and the additional two characteristic peaks at 796.70 and 781.46 eV correspond to Co3+. The characteristic peak of Co2+ exhibits a leftward shift of 0.29 eV relative to the precursor... The peaks at binding energies of 168.89, 164.00, and 161.83 eV are attributed to SO4^2-, S 2p1/2, and S 2p3/2

nodes.characterization_summary: Vibrational peaks compatible with Co3S4 crystal structure including Ag, Eg, and F2g modes, showing broadening and weakening related to morphological differences.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra revealed vibrational peaks that are highly compatible with the crystal structure of Co3S4, including Ag, Eg, and F2g (Supplementary Fig. 11)

nodes.characterization_summary: Higher electric field for n·Co3S4@NF needle-like structure compared to r·Co3S4@NF rod-like structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Kelvin probe atomic force microscopy experimentally confirmed that the electric field is higher for the n·Co3S4@NF with needle-like structure than the r·Co3S4@NF

nodes.characterization_summary: Zeta potential of n·Co3S4@NF is -24.5 mV, more negative than n·Co(OH)2@NF (30.4 mV), indicating weaker Cl- binding.

nodes.characterization_summary: 3D X-ray tomography shows n·Co3S4@NF maintains structural integrity after 24 h SOR stability test, unlike blank NF which shows cracks and sulfur deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Three-dimensional X-ray tomography images of the electrodes: h before and (i) after 24 h SOR stability test for blank NF; (j) before and (k) after 24 h SOR stability test for n·Co3S4@NF. It was observed that when driving the SOR with the conventional Ni foam... its skeleton structure showed cracks and sulfur deposition... When driving the SOR with n·Co3S4@NF, its skeleton showed structural integrity
